analysis.title: Tech selloff highlights rising scrutiny of AI spending (UBS House View - Daily EMEA)
key_insights: US tech led the market lower on Friday as questions about the AI buildout overshadowed strong 3Q earnings. Nasdaq Composite fell 2.9% on Friday and 2.0% on the week. S&P 500 fell 1.8% on Friday and 0.6% on the week.
UBS says earnings expectations are broadly being met, but investors now weigh three concerns more heavily: overinvestment, financing and cannibalization.
Alphabet kept its USD 195-205bn 2026 capex plan, reported negative free cash flow for the quarter and signaled a significant further capex increase for 2027. Shares fell almost 13% the following day.

Meta raised the lower end of its 2026 capex range to USD 135-145bn and pledged continued aggressive investment beyond 2026. Shares fell nearly 7% the following day on the higher capex floor and negative 3Q free cash flow.

Cloud growth is accelerating: Google Cloud revenue +103% y/y (82% prior quarter, 34% in the March quarter), Azure +48% (43% in the June quarter), Oracle +62% (47% before). All three guided to further cloud growth.
Microsoft reported an eight-fold increase in large Copilot accounts. Alphabet said Gemini reached 1 billion users.

Neocloud credit has sold off on a maturity and funding mismatch: large upfront debt-financed investment is supported by later cash flows that are sensitive to utilization, execution, customer renewal and refinancing.

Neoclouds are about 8% of UBS's capex estimate versus 80% for Alphabet, Amazon, Microsoft, Meta and SpaceX. UBS expects selective project delays, repricing and consolidation rather than a broad collapse in AI spending.
Alphabet's Search query growth hit a five-year high but Search revenue growth decelerated, as management said AI Mode currently monetizes at a lower rate.

Intel fell 28.6% on Friday. AI is boosting server orders but also causing component scarcity, so Intel could not fully meet data center demand. Scarcity has raised PC prices, which hurts its client business.
UBS raised aggregate AI capex forecasts to USD 1.0tr in 2026 and USD 1.4tr in 2027, and introduced USD 1.5tr for 2028.
UBS base case is that AI investment stays a positive driver of global equity returns in 2027, but higher volatility in the AI trade is likely to be the new normal.
Positioning advice: reduce single-stock concentration across the AI value chain, preferring foundry, compute and power. Rebalance across sectors and asset classes. Use volatility deliberately.
Preferred equity sectors are industrials, health care and financials. Preferred regions are the Eurozone, EM and Asia ex-Japan. High-quality fixed income rallied as stocks fell.

Brent rose to USD 118/bbl Friday on concerns the US may resume strikes on Iran, then fell more than 3% to below USD 110 Monday on extended Iran-Qatar talks. Nasdaq futures were up 0.9% and STOXX 50 futures up 0.3% at time of writing, and the KOSPI rebounded nearly 3%.

market_movers.rationale: Shares fell almost 13% after 3Q results on negative free cash flow and a signaled 2027 capex increase, though Google Cloud grew 103% y/y.
Shares fell nearly 7% after the 2026 capex range floor was raised to USD 135-145bn and 3Q free cash flow was negative.
Shares fell 28.6% Friday as component scarcity left it unable to fully meet data center demand and higher PC prices hurt the client business.

sector_views.rationale: Keep the AI theme but diversify across the value chain. Prefer foundry, compute and power plus financially strong platforms with pricing power.
Named as a preferred equity sector.

earnings_insights: Alphabet 3Q (reported): Google Cloud revenue +103% y/y vs +82% prior quarter. 2026 capex plan kept at USD 195-205bn, 3Q free cash flow negative, 2027 capex to rise significantly. Search revenue growth decelerated.
Meta 3Q (reported): lower end of 2026 capex range raised to USD 135-145bn, 3Q free cash flow negative.
Microsoft 3Q (reported): Azure +48% for the three months to September vs +43% for the June quarter.
Oracle (reported): cloud growth accelerated to 62% from 47%.
Intel (reported): shares fell 28.6% Friday on data center supply constraints from component scarcity and pressure on the client business.
Apple earnings are due 2 November (upcoming, no estimate given).

macro_indicators.interpretation: Fell 1bp Friday and 7bps on the week as quality bonds rallied during the equity selloff.
Rose on fears of renewed US strikes on Iran, then fell more than 3% on extended Iran-Qatar talks.
Listed as a data point to watch on 2 November, no figure given.

risk_factors: Overinvestment: negative free cash flow and rising capex floors at Alphabet and Meta.
Financing: neocloud maturity and funding mismatch, with cash flows sensitive to utilization, execution, customer renewal and refinancing.
Cannibalization: AI Mode monetizes at a lower rate than classic Search.
AI lab revenue growth slowing meaningfully, weaker cloud utilization, or falling AI costs failing to stimulate enough new usage.
Algorithmic efficiency sharply cutting compute needs, or large investments failing to deliver commensurate capability gains.
A significant deterioration in financial conditions limiting hyperscalers' willingness to fund new investment.
Component scarcity raising PC prices and hurting client hardware demand.
vol_and_positioning: UBS expects higher volatility in the AI trade to be the new normal at this stage of the cycle.
UBS advises investors to use volatility deliberately: decide responses in advance, rebalance, manage downside risk, generate income or build exposure gradually at predefined prices.
Single-name dispersion is evident within the North Asia AI supply chain despite the KOSPI rebound of nearly 3%.
geopolitical: Concerns that the US may resume military strikes against Iran lifted Brent to USD 118/bbl Friday.
Extended Iran-Qatar talks pulled Brent below USD 110/bbl on Monday.
